correctness.rationale: The full independent-edge minimum follows from automorphism averaging (convex largest and concave Fiedler eigenvalues), exact 2-by-2 corona spectral blocks, strict monotonicity of logarithmic elasticity, and the reciprocal identity F(4/z)=2F(z)/z. The unique symmetric optimum has x=2/sqrt(s ell), its budget scale is fixed, and the exact value follows by substitution. For cycles, equality in averaging and two independent sine/cosine Fiedler equations force each pendant and each rim conductance to its orbit value. The actual standalone verify.py was run and returned PASS 1522 Jacobi/formula/asymmetric checks; finite tests corroborate but do not prove the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The nearest exact published corona and sunlet solutions optimize the smallest positive eigenvalue alone, not its quotient with the largest eigenvalue; they are not implied by the present claim nor do they imply the reciprocal optimizer. The inspected Kempton-Herrmann-di Bernardo full paper addresses distributed optimization of the eigenratio on general networks but gives no exact sunlet/transitive corona solution. Corona spectral formulas and inverse-moment coherence theorems concern different objectives. Originality is best-knowledge only, with residual unindexed-priority risk.

value.rationale: The exact all-size solution of a widely used spectral conditioning objective is naturally motivated by fastest one-step mean-zero consensus contraction. It reveals a unique globally optimal design on every sunlet and a striking asymptotically twofold edge-priority disagreement with a published fastest spectral-gap solution; the resulting additive eigenratio regret grows as n/(2pi). Price-independence of optimal ratio is a structural consequence of homogeneous spectral scaling, rather than a contrived finite example.
